quotes.text: Our laws need to keep up with technology. The landscape of possibilities presented by artificial intelligence is changing rapidly. We must prioritize the rights of victims first, and protect women and children from new forms of violations and punish perpetrators for their actions.

My AI Safety Package consists of common-sense solutions to protect women and children from digital exploitation. [...] We must ensure we are working with, encouraging, and requiring tech companies to add necessary guardrails that protect vulnerable populations on the internet.

Technology evolves at a faster pace than we can legislate, and an AI moratorium would have stifled California’s ability to establish necessary oversight of AI and all the technologies it is embedded in.
Policy doesn't move as fast as technology, and we are seeing technology that could be utilized for a lot of good also be utilized to make things more expensive for the average person.

Proud to join Congressman Sam Liccardo and Mayor Matt Mahan at the #GovAI Summit — discussing how California can lead on AI with innovation, accountability, and fairness. 
I’m proud of work that shapes tech policy that works for people. 
#CaliforniaLeadership #FutureOfWork https://t.co/3gmzzVDLyV
When we’re talking about moratoriums, I think that’s the wrong move. [...] And the reason for that is because you can’t stop technology.

Our utilities companies are not going to prioritize the infrastructure improvements that they need to do, which is something that we have been having challenges with. And AI is the literal industrial revolution to all industries that we are talking about. And I think that there is a balancing act that we need to ensure when we are talking about a roadmap for both AI and data centers.
